canonical_title: OpenAI publishes ten mathematics and theoretical computer science advances from internal Astra model
aliases: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science
treatment: Treat as a major scientific-reasoning capability claim backed by an OpenAI publication, a 249-page manuscript collection, and public Lean certificates. Reinclude only for substantial independent mathematical validation or refutation, formal publication or peer review, corrections to specific results, or official Astra model release/model-card/API details.
known_facts: On August 1, 2026, OpenAI published ten claimed advances across mathematics and theoretical computer science produced by an internal version of Astra, which it described as its next major model.
OpenAI said the selected problems had been open with no progress on the main result for at least a decade in each case, and usually much longer.

The ten areas include high-dimensional sphere packing, binary and spherical codes, non-sofic groups, Connes's rigidity conjecture, arithmetic circuit complexity, quantum parallel repetition, closest vector problem hardness, Ehrhart's volume conjecture, multicolor Ramsey numbers, and extremal graph theory conjectures.
OpenAI published a 249-page manuscript collection describing the results.
OpenAI said Astra generated the mathematical arguments, humans used the same model to prepare manuscripts, and the model then formalized the arguments into Lean certificates.
OpenAI published the Lean certificates in the public GitHub repository openai/ten-proofs.
OpenAI estimated that the successful solution-generation token usage would cost roughly $2,000 at GPT-5.6 Sol API rates.

OpenAI explicitly said it takes responsibility for correctness while asking the mathematical community to evaluate the results and place them in context; broad independent validation was not yet established at first report.
reinclude_only_if: Independent domain experts validate, refute, or materially correct one or more of the ten results.
The results are accepted to major journals, conferences, or other formal mathematical publication venues, or substantial peer-review findings become public.
OpenAI issues corrections, withdrawals, or materially revised proofs or Lean certificates.
OpenAI officially releases Astra, publishes its model card, architecture/capability details, pricing, API availability, or ChatGPT access.
Independent evaluations establish whether Astra's research capability generalizes beyond these selected results.
notes: Official OpenAI publication and artifacts are verified. The existence of the manuscripts and Lean certificates is high confidence; the mathematical significance and correctness of all ten claimed advances still require independent expert validation.
